Hi Sara - great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum:

Recap (discovery highlights)
- Primary use case: structured extraction from support tickets + automated triage via function calls.
- Latency target: 150-200ms p95 for 512-token responses; throughput: ~150 requests/min initially.
- Data sensitivity: PII in tickets; customer requires SOC 2 + KMS support (you mentioned procurement will need evidence).

Recommended model profile (initial)
- redwood-llm-1.2 (our curated mid-sized model): best balance of cost and hallucination control for structured outputs.
- opt-6b-quant (4-bit): cost-efficient option for high-throughput scenarios; we'll compare quality vs latency.

What we'll deliver this week
- Baseline eval run against the prompt set you shared (attached: avery_prompt_set_v1.jsonl).
- Evaluation summary (attached: eval_results_summary.csv) with schema compliance metrics and field-level accuracy.
- Short doc with recommended model + config (attached: redwood_model_recommendations.pdf) and suggested retry/backoff settings for function/tool calls.

JSON schema & structured output items to confirm from your side
- Do you have a canonical JSON schema (JSON Schema draft preferred) for the function outputs we should validate against?
- Are there fields that can be relaxed (best-effort) vs required (must be exact)? This affects pass/fail thresholds.

Proposed next steps
1) You: confirm a) sample dataset access (or upload to the Drive link we shared), b) canonical JSON schema (if available), and c) procurement timeline/contacts.
2) We: run a focused eval (schema compliance + regression checks) across redwood-llm-1.2 and opt-6b-quant and return a short report with recommended config (retries, idempotency keys, backoff).
3) Align on a short pilot (2-4 weeks) if results look good.

Scheduling: I can block time for a 30-min follow-up next Wed/Thu. What works for you?

Thanks - attaching the initial artifacts and links.

Thanks for the ping, Marissa - looping in an outline of the eval we'll run once we get the canonical schema and the sample dataset. High-level plan:

1) Schema compliance checks (automated)
- Validate model outputs against customer JSON Schema (Draft-07 compatible).
- Produce per-field pass/fail and an overall schema match rate.
- Edge-case tests: missing fields, additional unexpected fields, array ordering where relevant.

2) Structured-output scoring & regression checks
- Field-level exact match for identifiers/keys; fuzzy match (normalized text) for free-text fields.
- Track regression vs their historical baseline (if provided) - flag any regressions >2% that could indicate model drift or prompt mismatch.

3) Function/tool-calling behavior & retries
- Simulate intermittent timeouts and confirm idempotency with backoff settings.
- Measure duplicate-action risk by issuing repeated calls with same idempotency key; recommend default retry policy (exponential backoff, 3 retries) and notes on server-side dedupe.

4) Model candidates & configs
- redwood-llm-1.2: default config for highest schema compliance; expected p95 latency ~160ms on pilot cluster (512 tokens).
- opt-6b-quant: cost-optimized; expected p95 latency ~120ms but may see ~3-5% lower schema match in early tests.

Deliverables & timeline
- 3 business days after receiving schema + sample dataset: initial eval report (schema match rates, field-level metrics, sample failure cases).
- +2 business days: tuned prompt/config suggestions & recommended retry/backoff policy.

Questions for Avery (to include in the Drive upload)
- Please confirm which fields are hard-required vs optional.
- Any existing idempotency key format you use for external calls?
- Are there any PII redaction rules we should apply at eval time?

I'll prepare a small reproducible test harness and share results in the Drive folder. If everyone agrees, I'll start as soon as the schema arrives.
